title: Just-In-Time (JIT) Engine
definition: The compiler engine introduced in Tailwind v3 that generates CSS instantly on-demand as you write it, rather than generating all 15MB of CSS upfront and purging it later.
simpleExplanation: Before JIT, Tailwind pre-built thousands of classes when you started your server, which took 5-10 seconds. With JIT, Tailwind builds absolutely nothing. When you type `bg-red-500` and hit save, the JIT engine detects it and compiles that ONE single CSS class in 3 milliseconds.
realWorldExample: JIT makes 'Arbitrary Values' possible. You can type `w-[314px]`. The JIT engine instantly reads it and compiles a custom CSS rule for 314 pixels on the fly.

basic: Do you need to manually enable the JIT engine in Tailwind v3+?
intermediate: How does the JIT engine change the way Tailwind handles variants like `focus:hover:md:text-red-500`?

answers.question: Manually enable?
answers.answer: No. JIT is the default and only engine in Tailwind v3 and above.

answers.question: Stacked variants?
answers.answer: Before JIT, generating every possible combination of variants would create gigabytes of CSS, so it was restricted. JIT generates them on-demand, meaning you can stack infinite variants (`md:focus-visible:hover:bg-red-500`) with zero file size penalty.
